title: Metadata-driven retention and query-performance profiles for audit logs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our current audit ingestion and retention is a one-size-fits-all policy (30d hot, 90d cold) which drives unnecessary storage cost for large tenants and keeps high-sensitivity events on hot storage longer than required. With RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML metadata we have richer context (role sensitivity, org classification, compliance tier) that should drive retention, indexing granularity, and partitioning.

Goal: Implement a metadata-driven retention & indexing profiles system that: 1) assigns a retention and indexing profile at ingest time based on SSO/RBAC-derived attributes, 2) creates query-performance profiles (indexing/compaction) per profile to improve typical audit queries, 3) surface cost forecasts for tenant-level retention decisions, and 4) integrate controls so admins can override profiles via console (admin controls) and have changes audited.

Scope:
- Ingestion path: enrich incoming audit events with SSO/SAML-derived org metadata and RBAC v2 role tags.
- Policy engine: small rules engine that maps metadata to: hot retention window, index granularity (full-text vs summarized), partition window, sampling rules for low-value events, and whether to store raw payloads in long-term cold archive.
- Storage orchestration: implement partition lifecycle transitions (hot->warm->cold) and compact/index strategies per profile.
- Observability & cost: add telemetry that projects 90d/365d cost per tenant under chosen profile and shows cost delta if admin overrides.
- Admin UX hooks: Console endpoints for admins to view and change a tenant profile; changes generate audit events and require RBAC checks.

Non-goals: Replacing global compliance retention (e.g., legal holds) or building full tenant billing integration in this ticket.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in storage spend for top 5 largest tenants within 60 days of rollout (projected via telemetry).
- 95th percentile query latency for the most common audit queries improves by 15% for high-sensitivity profiles.
- Admin override flow is audited and requires RBAC v2 approver flow when changing retention > 90d.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest enrichment pipeline attaches SSO/SAML org_id and RBAC_v2 role_tag to every audit event (end-to-end tested)
Policy engine v1 maps at least three profiles (high_sensitivity, standard, low_value) to retention and indexing actions and is configurable via a feature flag
Storage lifecycle controller routes partitions according to profile rules and triggers compaction/index jobs with profile-specific parameters
Cost forecasting dashboard displays per-tenant 90d and 365d estimates and shows delta for admin overrides
Console exposes a read/write API for tenant retention/profile changes; changes create audit events and are subject to RBAC checks
Integration tests that simulate a 10k eps tenant and validate retention transitions and query latencies under load
